title: Designing Charts People Understand in Five Seconds (blog explainer)

brief.story: A clear explainer of the post.

slides.title: Charts People Understand in Five Seconds
bullets: One chart, one message, five seconds
slides.notes: A chart on a slide has a few seconds to do its job. In a video, you can't point at the bar that matters, so the chart must explain itself.

slides.title: Start with the sentence, not the chart
bullets: Renewals rose every quarter after we changed onboarding
Support tickets fell by about half in the first month
Region B is now our largest market
slides.notes: Before you open the chart tool, write the one sentence you want people to remember. That sentence decides the chart type, what to highlight and what to cut.

slides.title: Pick the chart that fits the point
bullets: Comparing a few items: sorted bar chart
Ranking: horizontal bar, largest at top
A single key number: the number itself
slides.notes: Match the chart to your point, and when in doubt, use a bar chart. Sometimes the best chart is no chart, just forty hours a month in large type.

slides.title: Grey everything, colour one thing
bullets: Make every bar or line grey
Colour only the one that carries your message
Add a label beside the highlighted item
slides.notes: This is the biggest improvement you can make. The eye goes straight to the colour, and a direct label means people with colour vision deficiency get the message too.

slides.title: Cut clutter, state the takeaway
bullets: After: Renewals rose every quarter after the new onboarding
slides.notes: Label directly and cut the clutter. Then let the headline say what the chart shows, not what it is. Read the headline, see the proof, test passed.

slides.title: Turn data slides into a clear video
bullets: Say numbers the way people say them
Give each chart enough narration time
Pro: charts rebuilt as animated charts
Try Basic first, no subscription needed
slides.notes: Put the explanation in your speaker notes. On Pro, a.i. directs the video, rebuilding each chart so the highlight lands on its word. Try it at powerpoint2vid.com.
